recommended_actions: If any probe succeeded: remove the file from the web root, rotate every secret it contained (database passwords, API keys), and review access logs for other downloads of it.
Deny access to dot-files and backups in the web server configuration.
Block the IP if probing continues.
Block the IP at the reverse proxy or CDN.
Follow the runbook of any related alert that shows a successful request.
Consider rejecting requests with empty user agents on public routes, after checking that monitoring and API clients send one.
Make sure nothing sensitive is reachable: remove backups, old admin panels and test pages from the web root.
Block or rate-limit the IP if the scanning continues or is aggressive.
Return the same response for missing and forbidden paths where possible.
limitations: Enrichment not run: IP reputation and location were not considered
Single log source (access_log): no other log corroborates it
Possible benign cause for PRH-WEB-001: Search-engine crawlers following stale links
Possible benign cause for PRH-WEB-001: A broken page that references many missing assets
Possible benign cause for PRH-WEB-003: Health checks or scripts that send no user agent, such as an internal monitor
Possible benign cause for PRH-WEB-003: Vulnerability scans the site's own team runs on purpose
Possible benign cause for PRH-WEB-004: The site's own security scanner
Possible benign cause for PRH-WEB-004: Sites that really run WordPress or phpMyAdmin, where admins visit these paths
